# jq 1.7.1 — command-line JSON processor

Source: https://github.com/jqlang/jq/releases/download/jq-1.7.1/jq-1.7.1.tar.gz

- **Version**: 1.7.1
- **Author**: Stephen Dolan and the jq contributors
- **License**: MIT (see `COPYING`)
- **SHA-256** (release tarball): `478c9ca129fd2e3443fe27314b455e211e0d8c60bc8ff7df703873deeee580c2`

Bundled regex engine — **Oniguruma 6.9.9** (see `oniguruma/`):

- Source: https://github.com/kkos/oniguruma/releases/download/v6.9.9/onig-6.9.9.tar.gz
- **License**: BSD-2-Clause (see `oniguruma/COPYING`)
- **SHA-256**: `60162bd3b9fc6f4886d4c7a07925ffd374167732f55dce8c491bfd9cd818a6cf`

## Status

**Fully working — behaviourally identical to upstream `jq`.** The wasm binary
passes jq's entire official test corpus with the *same* score as the reference
clang build:

| suite            | wasm jq        | clang jq 1.7.1 |
| ---------------- | -------------- | -------------- |
| `jq.test`        | 435/447        | 435/447        |
| `man.test`       | 222/224        | 222/224        |
| `onig.test`      | 40/40          | 40/40          |
| `manonig.test`   | 17/17          | 17/17          |
| `base64.test`    | 7/7            | 7/7            |
| `optional.test`  | 3/3            | 3/3            |

(The handful of non-passing entries are the module/`import`/`modulemeta`
filesystem-fixture tests, which fail identically under clang jq when the module
directory is not on the search path — they are not port defects.)

```
$ printf '%s' '{"a":[1,2,3]}' | node host.js jq.wasm '.a[1]'
2
$ printf '"héllo"' | node host.js jq.wasm '[match("\\w";"g").string] | length'
5
```

### The oniguruma decision — BUNDLED

jq's `test`/`match`/`sub`/`scan`/`split(re;flags)` family needs a regex engine.
Oniguruma vendors cleanly under this repo's compiler + libc (it is ISO C; the
only build input autoconf normally supplies is a `config.h` of fixed target
facts, hand-written here as `oniguruma/config.h`), so it is **bundled** rather
than dropped — jq regex works fully (Perl syntax, named captures, Unicode
`\w`/`\p{...}`, case-insensitive and other flags). Only the core engine plus the
ASCII/UTF-8/Unicode encodings are compiled (jq runs UTF-8-only); the other
encodings, the POSIX/GNU API wrappers, and `mktable.c` are omitted. The
`unicode_*_data.c` tables are `#include`d by `unicode.c` (not separate TUs), so
they are present but not listed as sources.

## Build

```bash
node compiler.js -o /tmp/jq.wasm vendor/jq/bin.json
node host.js /tmp/jq.wasm '.'
```

Derived files committed alongside the sources (normally generated by jq's
build, reproduced here so no flex/bison/autoconf step is needed):

- `src/lexer.c` / `src/parser.c` — shipped pre-generated in the release tarball.
- `src/builtin.inc` — the jq-language builtin prelude, from `src/builtin.jq` via
  jq's Makefile recipe: `sed -e 's/\\/\\\\/g' -e 's/"/\\"/g' -e 's/^/"/' -e
  's/$/\\n"/' src/builtin.jq`.
- `src/config_opts.inc` — the `JQ_CONFIG` string (normally `./config.status
  --config`; a fixed banner here).
- `src/version.h` — shipped in the tarball (`JQ_VERSION "1.7.1"`).

## Local additions (not upstream)

- `pthread.h` — single-threaded TSD/once/mutex shim. The gucOS process model is
  single-threaded, so jv.c's decNumber context and jv_dtoa_tsd.c's dtoa context
  collapse to per-process globals. jq's real threading is `HAVE_PTHREAD`-gated
  and left off.
- `src/jq_gucos_shims.{c,h}` — **`strptime()` only**, which this repo's libc
  doesn't provide but jq's date builtins need. Still advertised via
  `-DHAVE_TIMEGM/-DHAVE_GMTIME_R/-DHAVE_STRPTIME`: all three are true, but the
  first two are now satisfied by the LIBC rather than by this TU.
  `timegm()` and `gmtime_r()` were dropped from here by **todos/0325 Group B /
  todos/0382 gap 5**, which added both to the libc — keeping the local copies
  became a duplicate-symbol link error. This is the outcome the file's own
  header note anticipated ("if a future compiler.js grows them, drop the
  define(s) and this TU can shrink").
- `oniguruma/config.h` — hand-written autoconf substitute (wasm32 ILP32 facts).

## Patch table (edits to upstream sources)

Everything else is verbatim upstream. All edits carry an inline `gucOS wasm
port:` comment.

| File            | Change | Why |
| --------------- | ------ | --- |
| `src/jv.h`      | add `#else` empty defs for `JV_PRINTF_LIKE`/`JV_VPRINTF_LIKE` | upstream defines them only under `__GNUC__`; this compiler isn't GNU, leaving the declarations that use them unparseable |
| `src/jv.h`, `src/compile.h` | wrap the `JV_ARRAY`/`JV_OBJECT`/`BLOCK` arg-count dispatch in a one-arg `*_PP_EXPAND(x) x` pass | this PP doesn't re-scan a macro name produced by an inner expansion when its `(...)` args come from the same replacement list; the extra pass forces the rescan |
| `src/util.h`    | `MIN`/`MAX` → portable ternary | upstream uses GNU statement-expressions `({...})` + `__typeof__` (unsupported); jq's only use passes side-effect-free args |
| `src/jv_file.c` | `const int` array bound → `enum` | a `const int` size is not an integer constant expression in C → VLA (unsupported) |
| `src/jv_alloc.c`| normalize zero-size `malloc`/`calloc`/`realloc` to 1 byte | this libc returns NULL for a zero-size request (C-legal); jq treats NULL as fatal OOM, assuming glibc's non-NULL-for-zero (e.g. a bytecode block with zero subfunctions) |
| `src/builtin.c` | `#include "jq_gucos_shims.h"` | pull in the date-shim prototypes |

## Build configuration (`bin.json` `-D` flags)

- `-DIEEE_8087` — little-endian IEEE (required by David Gay's dtoa).
- `-DUSE_DECNUM` — jq 1.7's decimal **literal preservation** (arbitrary-precision
  number literals round-trip exactly, matching upstream). decNumber is compiled
  in; without this flag jq silently degrades every number to `double`.
- `-DHAVE_LIBONIG` — enable the regex builtins against the bundled Oniguruma.
- `-DHAVE_CONFIG_H` — make Oniguruma include its `config.h`.
- `-DHAVE_ALLOCA_H`, `-DHAVE_ISATTY`, `-DHAVE_SETENV` — libc features present here.
- Date: `-DHAVE_STRFTIME/STRPTIME/TIMEGM/GMTIME_R/LOCALTIME_R/TM_TM_GMT_OFF`.
- Math: `-DHAVE_<FN>` for every libm function this repo's libc provides (acos …
  trunc) so the corresponding jq math builtins register as real (missing ones —
  `fma`, `remainder`, `scalbln`, `lgamma_r`, Bessel — stay unsupported).
